content.comment_body: Hello, Is there any way to save text labels and I/O names in the [product_name] controller, so I can recover them if I lose the original program? I've tried copying the program to the SD card, but this doesn't seem to work. When I upload the program to the PC, only the block names appear, not any text labels or I/O names. Kind regards, [user_name]
No, it's not possible to store comments directly on the [product_name]; they can only be stored within the [product_name] project file.

You can keep the source file and/or a PDF backup on a microSD card and insert it into the [product_name] device. This provides a backup, and if you're using ladder logic, it's easier to read the diagram from the file rather than by uploading from the device where it may look unclear. Regards, [user_name]
Thanks. What's the simplest way to save files to the SD card? Do I need to remove it from the [product_name] device and use a file manager on the PC? /[user_name]

The easiest method is to use a memory card reader and access the SD card directly from the PC. The SD card slot in the [product_name] device is mainly for backup purposes. Alternatively, you can use a USB stick and keep it near your [product_name] setup to prevent data loss from your PC. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users want the ability to retain descriptive data such as text and I/O labels directly on the controller for disaster recovery, but the hardware does not support saving such metadata. Current solutions involve storing files on external media like microSD cards or USB sticks, but these are workarounds rather than integrated features.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that the controller will support backing up all program documentation, including text and I/O names, within hardware backups so that a full restoration is possible.
